newsitem.title: USA: U.S. OPTIONS FOCUS/Big trade in Morris July calls.
newsitem.headline: U.S. OPTIONS FOCUS/Big trade in Morris July calls.

text.p: A large spread crossed in Philip Morris Cos Inc options Tuesday in what analysts said could be a bullish play.
The Philip Morris July 45 call traded about 11,625 contracts and the July 50 call traded 11,155.
In afternoon trading, the stock was down 1/8 at 42-3/4 on turnover of about 7.1 million shares.
"It's a pure bull spread," said Michael Schwartz, a managing director at Oppenheimer & Co, noting the open interest in the two options was relatively thin ahead of Tuesday's trade.
Through Monday, open interest in the July 45 calls was about 4,500 and in the July 50s about 6,565.

Schwartz said the bull spread could have been done to take advantage of any potential stock rally if a settlement is reached between tobacco companies and the states that are suing them to recoup Medicaid costs of smokers.
On Tuesday, a key negotiator in the tobacco settlement talks said he expected meetings between the industry, state attorneys general and public health officials to drag on for days.
"It's a move you make if you're expecting a tremendous move in the stock," Harrison Roth, a first vice president at Cowen & Co, said of the Philip Morris July 45/50 spread.
He said the spread was not a dividend capture play.
Philip Morris options typically trade extremely heavily around the stock's ex-dividend date, which this quarter falls on Thursday.
"It's not dividend-related," Schwartz agreed. "The dividend is not until the 12th (of June), so those dividend spreads won't go on until tomorrow and those are usually deep in-the-money."
Among other Philip Morris options, the June 42-1/2 call was most active, with turnover of 3,215 contracts.
The July 40 put traded about 1,540 contracts and the June 40 put traded 1,215.
